content.text:
**Finding: compliant** (§ 9.4, paragraph p0039) — no redline proposed.

§ 9.4 sits at the **preferred** position on every material term of T4C:

| Rule element | § 9.4 |
|---|---|
| Customer convenience right | Yes — Agreement or any Order Form, in whole or in part |
| Notice period | 30 days' prior written notice (preferred) |
| Early-termination fee | None; Fees owed only for conforming Services through the effective date |
| Pro-rata refund | Yes — Vendor must promptly refund prepaid Fees for the post-termination period |
| Vendor convenience right | Expressly excluded during a committed term |

I verified by document-wide search that no Vendor convenience or at-will exit right sits elsewhere: §§ 9.1–9.2 are mutual breach/insolvency rights, § 9.3 is an additional Customer cause right, and § 24.4 bars Vendor from terminating on our change of control. This clause benefits us, so it should not be touched.

One cross-reference worth carrying forward, but deliberately **not** flagged under this rule: § 2.1's three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay applies "without reduction or termination rights," which is in tension with § 9.4 and could be argued to undercut the refund economics. That is the minimum-commitment bargain and belongs to the MINCOMMIT rule — flagging it here would double-count the same commercial term. Note that § 2.2's order-of-precedence ladder does not resolve the § 2.1 / § 9.4 conflict, so when MINCOMMIT is negotiated it is worth adding an express carve-out making the commitment subject to § 9.4.
